entries.context: \paragraph{Appearance and learned visual cues.} Domain randomization varies simulated appearance to improve transfer \citep{Tobin2017Domain,Tremblay2018Training}. Texture--shape cue conflicts reveal that models can rely on visual evidence different from that used by humans \citep{Geirhos2019Texture}. Our intervention targets an operational source of appearance variation: changing a scene's material representation while retaining its geometry. This lets us examine localization and navigation decisions under a concrete transformation encountered when simulation assets are reused.

entries.advisory_evidence_summary: Randomizes textures, lighting, cameras and distractors in synthetic object-localization images; evaluates transfer to real images.

entries.context: \paragraph{Grounding and model readout.} Shikra and Ferret integrate referring and grounding with language generation \citep{Chen2023Shikra,You2024Ferret}. Molmo explicitly develops pointing data, Qwen2.5-VL supports object localization and dynamic image resolution, and InternVL3 explores multimodal training and inference recipes \citep{Deitke2024Molmo,Bai2025Qwen,Zhu2025InternVL}. These capabilities make spatial outputs useful, but the interface through which a point is emitted also becomes part of the experiment. Prompt dependence is well established for language models \citep{Zhao2021Calibrate}; we examine its interaction with a paired visual intervention and separate executable output from conditional localization accuracy.
entries.source_locator: Introduction PDF p. 2; Section 3 pp. 4–5
entries.advisory_evidence_summary: Represents spatial coordinates as numerical text and combines spatial referring, grounding and dialogue in one multimodal model.

entries.context: \paragraph{Embodied evaluation.} Vision-and-language navigation couples language understanding to sequential perception and action \citep{Anderson2018Vision}. GRUtopia provides interactive scenes and tasks for embodied research \citep{Wang2024GRUtopia}; DualVLN combines grounding and control in a navigation system \citep{Wei2026Ground}. We use GRScenes for point-level experiments and KuJiaLe scenes for paired navigation. The common experimental question is how a change to rendered appearance alters decisions, from one image to an entire episode.

entries.advisory_evidence_summary: Defines visually grounded navigation as a sequence of actions that changes observations while following language instructions.
